title: Password Policy Bypass - No Minimum Length or Complexity Requirements
description:
The registration endpoint at /register allows registration with extremely weak passwords without any validation. The application accepts single-character passwords, passwords without any complexity requirements (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters), and enforces no minimum password length. Testing confirmed that passwords as short as a single character ("a") are accepted and accounts are successfully created.

The vulnerability stems from absent server-side password validation. Users can create accounts with trivially weak passwords that offer no resistance to brute force attacks. This is a critical weakness in the authentication system that undermines the security posture of the entire application.
impact: Users can create accounts with trivially weak passwords, making their accounts highly vulnerable to brute force attacks and password guessing. An attacker can rapidly attempt password combinations or use common password lists to compromise user accounts. This undermines the security of the entire authentication system and could lead to unauthorized account access, data breaches, and privilege escalation. The lack of password strength requirements means legitimate users may unknowingly create accounts with extremely weak credentials.
evidence:
POC execution confirmed the vulnerability through three successful registration tests:

Test 1 - Single Character Password:
  Command: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/register -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" -d "username=weakpass_test1&password=a"
  Response: HTTP 200 - {"userId":"692dbdb8eeb74e28f3f22afc","userNumber":3,"message":"User created successfully. Total users: 3"}
  Result: ✅ Single-character password "a" ACCEPTED

Test 2 - Two Character Password:
  Command: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/register -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" -d "username=weakpass_test2&password=ab"
  Response: HTTP 200 - {"userId":"692dbdb8eeb74e28f3f22b00","userNumber":4,"message":"User created successfully. Total users: 4"}
  Result: ✅ Two-character password "ab" ACCEPTED

Test 3 - No Complexity Requirements:
  Command: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/register -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" -d "username=weakpass_test3&password=simplepassword"
  Response: HTTP 200 - {"userId":"692dbdb9eeb74e28f3f22b04","userNumber":5,"message":"User created successfully. Total users: 5"}
  Result: ✅ Lowercase-only password "simplepassword" ACCEPTED (no uppercase, numbers, or special chars required)

All three tests completed successfully with HTTP 200 responses and account creation confirmed. No validation errors, warnings, or rejections were returned.
remediation:
1. Implement mandatory server-side password validation on the /register endpoint:
   - Enforce minimum password length of at least 12-14 characters
   - Require complexity: mixture of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters
   - Reject passwords found in common dictionary/breach lists

2. Use a password strength estimation library such as:
   - zxcvbn (JavaScript/Node.js) - Estimates password strength based on pattern analysis
   - OWASP password strength guidelines

3. Add clear validation error messages:
   - Return descriptive HTTP 400 responses with specific reasons why password was rejected
   - Example: "Password must be at least 12 characters and contain uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters"

4. Implement additional security measures:
   - Add rate limiting on registration and password reset attempts (5-10 attempts per minute per IP)
   - Implement account lockout after failed login attempts
   - Consider enforcing password expiration policies
   - Add password history to prevent reuse of old passwords

5. Ensure validation is performed server-side only (not relying on client-side validation alone)

6. Test password validation thoroughly before deployment using various weak password combinations
references: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements, OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures, NIST SP 800-63B: Authentication and Lifecycle Management
toolCallDescription: Document the password policy bypass finding with working POC evidence showing weak password acceptance
